learn.title: Pick the smallest
learn.body: Selection sort builds the sorted part from the left. Find the smallest item in the unsorted part, swap it into the first unsorted place, and then do the same on what is left.

learn.title: Selection sort on {64, 25, 12, 22, 11}
learn.body: Each step finds the smallest remaining item and swaps it to the front of the unsorted part.
steps: Smallest of the rest is 12. Swap with 25: 11 12 25 22 64
Smallest of the rest is 22. Swap with 25: 11 12 22 25 64
Only 25 and 64 remain, already in order. Done

learn.title: Selection sort in C
learn.body: `m` remembers the index of the smallest item seen. The inner loop searches, the swap places it.

learn.title: The cost
learn.body: The inner loop always scans the whole unsorted part, so for 5 items it makes 4, 3, 2 and 1 comparisons: 10 in total. Even a sorted array costs the same. It is $\Theta(n^2)$. It makes at most one swap per round, so few swaps.
Selection sort is a good choice only when swapping is costly, because it moves each item at most once.

questions.prompt: What does selection sort do each round?
choices: Finds the smallest unsorted item and swaps it into place
questions.explanation: It selects the minimum of the unsorted part.

questions.prompt: `{64, 25, 12, 22, 11}`. After the first round, what is the first item?
questions.explanation: The smallest item, 11, is swapped into the first place.

questions.prompt: After the first round on `{64, 25, 12, 22, 11}` the array is...
questions.explanation: 11 and 64 swapped places. Nothing else moved.

questions.prompt: In selection sort the variable `m` stores the \_\_ of the smallest item found so far.
questions.explanation: Storing the index lets the swap use `a[m]` later.

questions.prompt: How many comparisons does selection sort make for 5 items?
An already sorted array is given to selection sort. How much work does it do?
choices: The same $n^2$ shape as any other input
questions.explanation: It still scans the whole unsorted part every round, so its comparisons never shrink.

questions.prompt: Match each sort to its big idea.
pairs: swap neighbours that are out of order
pick the minimum and swap it forward
questions.explanation: Both are quadratic, but they move items differently.
